The '''''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer''', also known as the '''''Imperial II''-class Destroyer''' and colloquially the '''ImpStar Deuce''', was a [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] model that was derived from the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer]].

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|Have you ever seen what a Star Destroyer can do to the surface of an unshielded planet? Stones run like water and sand turns to glass.|[[Carnor Jax]] to [[Mirith Sinn]].|<ref name="CE4">[[Crimson Empire 4|''Crimson Empire'' 4]]</ref>}}
[[File:ISD_schematic_EGVV.png|thumb|left|200px|''Imperial II''-class Destroyer technical drawing]]
Several differences existed between the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial I'']] and [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II'']]-class [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]], including the replacement of the [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] targeting array between the command tower's [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] globes with a communications tower, as well as the removal of point defense weaponry.

The ''Imperial II'' was built with a heavily reinforced hull, stronger [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]], and greater firepower than the original ''Imperial I'' class. The prominent quad heavy [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolaser]] and heavy [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]] turrets flanking the surface of the ''Imperial I''-class Star Destroyer were also replaced with batteries of eight-barreled turbolasers or ions in unarmored barbette [[Octuple barbette turbolaser|mountings]]. Another new feature included two parallel "claws" for grappling smaller [[Starship/Legends|starships]] placed in the ventral secondary docking bay.<ref name="TESB" />

During the height of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]], an Alliance Special Operations man said that the Star Destroyer had 174,000 design flaws waiting to be exploited.<ref name="SOTP">''[[Specter of the Past]]''</ref> The [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|command deck]] was also a vulnerability, as the ship's operations were coordinated there.<ref name="RS II guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref> Removal of point defense weapons was perhaps the greatest issue, due to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance's]] heavy use of starfighters.

Despite these flaws as well as the vast resources required to maintain and crew the vessels, they nevertheless remained formidable front line units, even when compared to more efficient and modern designs such as the [[Nebula-class Star Destroyer|''Nebula''-class]] and [[Turbulent-class Star Destroyer|''Turbulent''-class Star Destroyers]].

==History==
{{Quote|Sir, we're having trouble apprehending Moff Kalast. His star destroyer is one of the newer models, and we've been unable to succesfully engage him before he enters hypersapce|An Imperial officer to Grand Moff Tarkin, regading the now rebel controlled Imperial-II ''Avenger''|<ref name="EaW" />}}
[[File:ImpStarDuece-SWA.jpg|thumb|left|200px|An ''Imperial II'' unleashes a barrage of turbolaser fire.]]
The class began with the prototype ''Imperial II'' known as the [[Empire (Imperial II prototype)|''Empire'']], commanded by [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Feyet Kiez]]. The vessel was more powerful than later vessels of the line and was said to have amassed a reputation similar to that of the [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']]. The first operational ships of this class began to appear in service shortly before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="DSn" />

Among the first Imperial II star destroyers used in the prelude to Yavin was the [[Avenger/Legends|''Avenger'']], which was placed under the command of [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Kalast]], would fall under rebel control after Kalast learned of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|Death Star I]]'s construction and chose to defect to the Rebel Alliance, leaking the Death Star's existance through the [[Bothan Spynet/Legends|Bothan Spynet]]. Following a [[Battle at Jabiim|battle]] against rebel forces on [[Jabiim/Legends|Jabiim]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] would learn of Kalast's defection, leading an Imperial fleet against Kalast's ''Avenger'' over the planet [[Atzerri/Legends|Atzerri]]. While the warships of the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|rebel fleet]] were destroyed in the ensuing battle, the more advanced hyperdrive aboard Kalast's Imperial II allowed him to flee the battle. In response to this, Vader would deploy [[Immobilizer 418 Interdictor-class Heavy Cruiser|Immobilizer 418 cruisers]] among his forces so that when Kalast's Imperial II was encountered again escorted by another force of rebel ships, he would be unable to escape, allowing the Empire to damage the ''Avenger'' enough to recapture it and arrest Kalast for his treason.<ref name="EaW" />

[[File:Capture_of_Kalast.jpg|thumb|left|180px|One of the first ''Imperial II'' destroyers, the ''Avenger'', fell under rebel control, though it would be recaptured by Darth Vader.]]

Many participated at the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], including the ''Avenger'' and ''[[Stalker/Legends|Stalker]]''. During the final years of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] under [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] rule, this starship was instrumental in the implementation of the [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]].

The class also participated in the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]<ref name="RS II">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]''</ref> in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> and three Destroyers had their barbette mountings destroyed by [[Arvel Crynyd/Legends|Arvel Crynyd]] to protect the Rebel cruiser [[Home One/Legends|''Home One'']].<ref name="RS III">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>

The class remained in service for a significant length of time, despite more advanced starship designs being available. These warships were seen even during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], being used for both offensive and defensive roles in critical missions. However, use of the Imperial II was not limited solely to the military.

<div style="float:right">[[File:ISDIIESB.png|thumb|left|200px|An ''Imperial II'' being eclipsed by the [[Executor/Legends|Executor]].]]</div>
During the events of the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], the class remained operational, as [[Darth Caedus|Jacen Solo]] commanded the [[Anakin Solo (starship)|''Anakin Solo'']], a heavily upgraded and modified vessel which was in the service of the [[Galactic Alliance Guard]].

When the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] finally entered the war, it was able to field a fleet of these vessels, showing the type's prolonged service to the Empire. [[Supreme Commander]] [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]], however, chose the [[Bloodfin (Star Destroyer)|''Bloodfin'']], a newly built [[Turbulent-class Star Destroyer|''Turbulent''-class Star Destroyer]], as the Imperial flagship.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:MC80svsISD.png|thumb|left|Comparison between the [[MC80 Liberty Type Heavy Star Cruiser/Legends|MC80 ''Liberty'' type Star Cruiser]] and the ''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer.]]
The most prominent weapons on the second Star Destroyer model that appears in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']] are eight barbette mountings, each mounting eight gun-barrels, which are arranged in rows of four on either side of the superstructure. They replace the heavy turbolasers and heavy ion cannons on the ISD-I.

Numerous [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] sources cite the armament of the ''Imperial II'' as consisting of 50 turbolasers, heavy turbolasers or turbolaser batteries, and ion cannons.

At present, there is no [[canon]] source defining how the visible guns on the model relate to the armament stated in secondary sources, but the most likely estimation is that they correspond to weapons-distribution similar to earlier models like the ''Imperial I''-class and the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class]]. The guns on each side of the superstructure would then be the heaviest.
